annotations.title: How often haue they exaſperated.
annotations.text: Moyſes (Deu 9. v. 7.) repeting what had paſſed in the deſert, chargeth the people that they had ſtil prouoked our lord to wrath, <mn>[1]</mn> from the day, that they came out of Egypt, and always contended againſt him. And our lord himſelf expoſtulating their ingratitude, & often murmuring ſaith (Num. 14. v. 22.) in the beginning of the ſecond yeare, that they had then tempted him tenne times; <mn>[2]</mn>either by this certaine number ſignifying an vncertaine, or els chiefly tenne times: for ſo often we find recorded that they tempted him, and murmured within that ſmal time more notorionly. Firſt <mn>[3]</mn>nere, vnto the redde ſea (Exod. 14. v. 11.) where ſeing the Egyptians purſuing them, they murmured againſt Moyſes, for bringing them out of Egypt, ſaying: It had benne much better to haue ſerued the Egyptians, then to die in the wildernes. Secondly, <mn>[4]</mn>for want of ſwete water. Exod. 15. v. 24. Thirdly, <mn>[5]</mn>for lack of meate, Exod. 16. v. 3. Fourtly, <mn>[6]</mn>keeping Manna for the next day, contrarie to Gods commandment. ibid. v. 20. Fiftly, <mn>[7]</mn>going on the Sabbath day, alſo contrarie to Gods commandment, to gether Manna. Ibid. v. 27. Sixtly, <mn>[8]</mn>for want of water in Raphidim. Exod. 17. v. 2. Num. 26. v. 2 Seuently <mn>[9]</mn> in Horeb, adoring a calfe & the image therof. Exod. 32 Eightly, <mn>[10]</mn> repyning for their trauels in the wildernes. Nu. 11. v. 1. Nintly, <mn>[11]</mn> loathing Manna, and burning with deſire to eate fleſh. Ibid. v. 4. 5 6. Tently, <mn>[12]</mn> deſparing to poſſeſſe the promiſed land of Chanaan, after that the diſcouerers had reported the difficulties, with the force of the people, and of the cities againſt which they muſt fight. Nr. 14. v. 1. Al which and the reſt, ſaith S. Paul, happened to them in figure of vs: and are written for our correption (or admonition) that we murmur not as they did. 1. Cor. 10.

notes.text: The people of Israel often murmured in the desert.
The people of Israel often murmured in the desert. Tenne times more notoriously.
